title: People Behind the Settlements
dek: The officials, tradespeople, caregivers and witnesses whose work makes Fenumion a lived-in world.
sources: Public NPC dossiers; primary scene anchors in each recovered record
body:
A settlement survives through more than its battles. These histories follow the people who count votes, keep shops, carry water, provide care and remember what the community has lived through.

Find NPCs by island, or read the work and relationships that connect them below.

Decisions and their record

  • Hawthorne — The scribe who turns Pristinia’s arguments into counted votes, recorded decisions and an institutional memory.
  • Vizsla, the Florist — A flower-shop owner who argues that adventurers’ contributions should be recognized without displacing the settlement’s residents.
  • Hiram — An Elder whose arguments expose the tension between financial survival, political continuity and local defense.
  • Kaja — An Elder who resists solving Pristinia’s financial crisis by concentrating control in a few hands.
  • Magda — The Elder who announces a collective decision while keeping ordinary hospitality and its cost in view.
  • Orrik the Wheelwright — A resident whose suspicion of adventurers coexists with concrete proposals for changing how Pristinia is governed.

The work of survival

  • Farmer Scarlett — A Pristinian civilian whose wartime work makes survival a matter of water, bedding, labor and space.
  • Guardian Commander Yvette — A commander whose account of loyal soldiers and their graves gives institutional service a human cost.
  • Stella & Sola — The sisters whose shop links Pristinia’s ordinary comforts, medicine and emergency care.
  • Vance the Guard — An Eovar guard whose answers preserve one local view of commerce, privacy and suspicion.

Teaching, hospitality and witness

  • Papirak — teaching, loss and the institutions that survive him.
  • Herb — the Common Man and ordinary continuity.
  • Scout Lilian — reconnaissance and the cost of warning.
  • Murr the Old Wolf — Voraketh’s living memory.
  • Kvethe and Babel’s survivors — a community that speaks for itself.
  • Huoth — service and political testimony.
